title: Add forgot / reset password
learnerProfile: Writes Java and Python confidently. Can read JavaScript but would not write a React page or an Express route from scratch. Demos this feature to a teammate who will maintain it.

public.request: Add forgot password and reset password to the app. Email the user a link, let them set a new password from it.
public.conventions: Client pages live in client/src/pages and are auto-registered by filename, so adding a page needs no routing change. Pages never call fetch directly: every server call goes through a helper in client/src/api. On the server, HTTP endpoints are declared in server/routes, the logic for them lives in server/controllers, and anything persisted is a field on a model in server/models. Cross-cutting checks live in server/middleware. Email is sent through server/lib/mailer.js.

changes.role: declares POST /auth/forgot and POST /auth/reset, and wires the rate limiter onto the first of them
forgot() makes a random token, saves a hash of it plus a one-hour expiry on the user, and emails the link; reset() checks the hash and the expiry, sets the new password and clears the token

mechanismKeyPoints.statement: The page does not call the server directly; it goes through the helper in client/src/api/auth.js.
mechanismKeyPoints.why: It is the convention in this repo, so it is where a maintainer looks for the request.

mechanismKeyPoints.statement: The token is generated on the server, in the controller, not in the browser.
mechanismKeyPoints.why: A token the client could make is a token anyone could forge.

mechanismKeyPoints.statement: What is stored on the user is a hash of the token, not the token itself.
mechanismKeyPoints.why: If the database leaks, the stored value cannot be used to reset anyone's password.

mechanismKeyPoints.statement: The token is stored with an expiry, one hour by default.
mechanismKeyPoints.why: It stops an old link in an inbox from working forever.

mechanismKeyPoints.statement: The reset page gets the token from the URL of the emailed link.
mechanismKeyPoints.why: It is how the second request proves it is the same person who asked.

concepts.name: Express middleware
concepts.prereqQuestion: Before I explain it - do you know what Express middleware is?
concepts.shortExplanation: It counts requests per IP and returns 429 once there have been six in fifteen minutes, so nobody can spam reset emails at an address.
concepts.longExplanation: Think of it as a checkpoint. Every request to /auth/forgot passes through rateLimit before it ever reaches the controller. If that IP has already made six requests in the last fifteen minutes, the checkpoint answers 429 itself and the controller never runs.

analogies.java: It is the same idea as a servlet filter: it sees the request before the handler does and can reject it.
analogies.python: It is like a Flask before_request hook, or a decorator wrapped around the view.
analogies.c: It is like a guard clause at the top of a function that returns early on bad input, except it lives outside the function and runs for every request to that route.
analogies.default: It is a checkpoint the request passes through before the handler, and it can turn the request away.

concepts.name: Storing a hash instead of the token
concepts.prereqQuestion: Quick one before I go on - do you know why you would store a hash of a token rather than the token?
concepts.shortExplanation: Same reason as passwords: if the database leaks, a hash cannot be replayed.
concepts.longExplanation: The emailed link carries the raw token. The database only keeps its hash. When the reset page sends the token back, the server hashes it again and compares. So a stolen database row cannot be turned into a working reset link.

analogies.default: It is the same reason you never store a password in plain text.

finalCheck.question: Last one. To change how long a reset link stays valid, from one hour to six, which file do you edit?
finalCheck.answerDetail: in forgot(), the line that sets user.resetTokenExpiry to Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000

distractors.note: It stores resetTokenExpiry, but it does not decide the value. Storing and setting are different jobs, and that is the distinction a maintainer needs.
That is the fifteen minute rate limit window, which is a different clock from the token expiry.
